MSFT.rationale: MSFT presents a strong fundamental case: 18.3% YoY revenue growth, 23.4% YoY EPS growth, 46.3% operating margins, $46.7B quarterly OCF, and a fortress balance sheet with $38B net cash. The franchise is best-in-class with deep moats across Azure, M36, and LinkedIn. Valuation has compressed significantly — PE from 40.4x to 27.2x, EV/EBIT from 32.1x to 20.5x — while fundamentals have improved, placing the stock near the bottom of its 1-year valuation range. The Q4 FY2026 earnings report on July 29 is a credible near-term catalyst: consensus is modest ($4.21-4.24 EPS, ~$87.6B revenue), and a beat-and-raise on Azure growth and Copilot adoption could trigger re-rating. Offsetting factors cap the score below +0.5: the 10-year yield at 4.71% exceeds MSFT's 3.7% earnings yield by ~100bp, creating a structural headwind on justified multiples; the QoQ EPS decline of -17.2% (Q2 to Q3) warrants monitoring though likely reflects Q2 noise rather than structural deterioration; and the Copilot class-action lawsuits and AI capex scrutiny add uncertainty. The PE path was broadly but not monotonically declining (partial reversion Feb-May 2026), so the compression narrative is directionally correct but not as clean as a straight-line decline. On balance, a durable franchise at a cyclical discount with a dated catalyst justifies a moderately positive score.
